labels.text: the shop collects it and sends it on

scenes.vo: Your bill says GST. The shop collects it and the shop sends it to the government. So the shopkeeper pays GST out of his own pocket. True or false?

spec.title: Who really pays a tax?
spec.sub: GST and the rest, part one

scenes.vo: The law and your wallet give two different answers. This is the puzzle of who really pays a tax.
This part is the economics. Part two is how the Constitution made GST possible. Part three is the money.

labels.text: NCERT: a compulsory payment to the government
ART. 265 · no tax without authority of law

scenes.vo: Start with what a tax is. NCERT calls it a compulsory payment to the government. It pays for schools, hospitals, roads and defence. And Article two hundred sixty-five says no tax can be collected except by authority of law.

Why does a government tax at all? NCERT gives the Budget three jobs. Allocation pays for goods the market cannot provide, which NCERT calls public goods, like national defence and roads. Redistribution moves income through taxes and transfers. Stabilisation steadies the economy when demand rises or falls too fast.
Taxes come in two families. A direct tax is paid on your income or profits, like income tax. An indirect tax is added to the price of goods and services, like GST.

labels.text: IMPACT · who hands it to the government
direct: the same person · indirect: can differ

scenes.vo: But that line hides the real question. Economists separate impact from incidence. Impact is who hands the tax to the government. Incidence is who finally bears it. For a direct tax they are the same person. For an indirect tax they can be different people.

labels.text: CGST Act: the taxable person pays
CBIC: the final consumer is to bear it

scenes.vo: So back to the shop. The CGST Act says the tax shall be paid by the taxable person. In the usual case, that is the supplier. But CBIC's own FAQ says the burden of GST is to be borne by the final consumer. So the answer is false. The shop pays by law. In design, you bear it in the price.

labels.text: IGNOU: buyers buy a little less
the price rises by less than the tax
the split depends on how easily each can walk away

scenes.vo: But can the shop always pass on the whole tax? Not always. IGNOU shows that when a tax pushes the price up, buyers buy a little less. So the whole rise need not be passed on. The price rises by less than the tax, and the seller absorbs the rest. How the burden splits depends on how easily buyers and sellers can walk away.

labels.text: PROGRESSIVE · higher rate as income rises

scenes.vo: Taxes also differ by who carries more of the weight. A progressive tax takes a higher rate as income rises. A proportional tax takes the same rate. A regressive tax takes a falling rate as income rises. India's personal income tax is progressive. People below a limit pay nothing.

labels.text: NCERT, IGNOU: indirect taxes are called regressive
the same rupees: a bigger share of a smaller income

scenes.vo: But what about GST? NCERT calls indirect taxes regressive, because they hit all income groups equally. IGNOU also calls them regressive. Here is our reading. The same tax in rupees is a bigger share of a smaller income. A poorer family spends a larger share of its income on everyday purchases. So a tax in the price tends to take a bigger share of it.

labels.text: a subsidy: the State pays so something costs less
the Budget's total includes the States' share of taxes

scenes.vo: Money flows the other way too. In plain words, a subsidy is money the State puts in so that something costs less. NCERT says some are open, on food or fertiliser. Others are hidden, when public goods like education and health are priced low. In the twenty twenty-six to twenty-seven Budget's rupee chart, major subsidies are six paise of every rupee.

Now the old problem that GST was built to fix. Why did a pen once carry more tax than it should? Follow one pen, using CBIC's own example. The maker's inputs cost ten rupees and carry one rupee of excise. The pen sells for twenty rupees plus two rupees of excise. That is twenty-two.

labels.text: excise could not be set off against State VAT

scenes.vo: But then the State's VAT was charged on the whole twenty-two rupees. That includes the two rupees of central tax. So a tax was charged on a tax. NCERT calls this cascading. NCERT says the old system gave minimal credit for tax paid on inputs. In the pen example, excise could not be set off against State VAT.

labels.text: CREDIT for the tax paid before
only the value added is taxed
NCERT: a tax on value addition

scenes.vo: GST fixes this with a credit chain. Tax is paid at every stage, but each seller gets credit for the tax already paid before. So only the value added at each stage is taxed. NCERT calls it effectively a tax on value addition.

GST is also a destination tax. The revenue goes to the place where the goods are consumed, CBIC says. So it is split two ways. Inside a State, the Centre levies CGST and the State levies SGST. That is why one bill can show two taxes. Across States, the Centre levies IGST and shares it.

But not everything is inside GST. Alcohol for drinking is outside by the Constitution's own definition. CBIC's FAQ also keeps electricity out. And five petroleum products, including petrol and diesel, wait for the GST Council to set a date.

labels.text: NCERT Class XI Statistics: a weighted mean
OLD RATES · the method is the point

scenes.vo: Now test the idea with numbers, a game from NCERT's own statistics book. A family spends on five groups of goods at five GST rates. What is its average GST rate? NCERT works it out as a weighted mean, about nine point six six per cent. Those were the old rates. The point is the method. The more you spend at a rate, the more it counts.

labels.text: IN THE PRICE · you bear it
how much passes on depends on buyers and sellers

scenes.vo: So who really pays a tax? By law, the shop pays GST to the government. In the price, you bear it. And how much the shop can pass on depends on how buyers and sellers respond.

lines.text: impact v incidence: who pays v who bears
direct taxes stay; indirect taxes shift
cascading was tax on tax; GST credits earlier tax, at the destination

scenes.vo: For the exam, write it this way. Separate impact from incidence. Direct taxes land where they fall; indirect taxes shift. Indirect taxes are called regressive. Cascading was tax on tax, and GST's credit chain taxes only value added, at the destination.
But one tax shared by the Centre and every State needed the Constitution itself to change. That is part two.
